raw.deadline_display: In most cases, you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.

source.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture (Erasmus+ programme site)
source.as_of: Page last updated 26 June 2025; describes the annual intake cycle generically, with no cycle-specific year
source.raw_extract:
When to apply

A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year.

In most cases, you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.

Each master's website has all the details about the course of study, the list of the participating universities, the entry requirements and all the steps of the application process (with and without scholarship).
source.exact_deadline_wording: In most cases, you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.
source.notes: Official European Commission programme page for EMJM. Independently corroborated by the EACEA catalogue page, which uses the same October-January window, so there is no conflict. Students apply directly to each consortium; per-programme deadlines are set by each master's own website and are not published by the European Commission.

source.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture (Erasmus+ programme site)
source.as_of: Page last updated 18 December 2025
source.raw_extract:
How to apply

There's no central application form to study abroad with Erasmus+.

You can reach out to the international or Erasmus+ office of your university or higher education institution to start the process.

Your sending higher education institution is obliged to select applicants in a fair and transparent way.
source.exact_deadline_wording: (none - the page states no deadline, no application window and no rolling basis)
source.notes: The official page confirms there is no central EU-level application route, but it never uses the words rolling, year-round or no fixed deadline, and it gives no application window. Brief section 6 allows ROLLING only where the source explicitly says rolling / no fixed deadline, so this stays UNKNOWN rather than being upgraded to ROLLING. The shard's stated 'typically 1-3 months before departure' was not confirmed by any official page and was not written. Each sending institution publishes its own Erasmus+ selection deadlines per academic year, which are not derivable from any EU-level page.

source.raw_extract:
Application and selection criteria – bachelor level

To be considered for the scholarship you simply apply for admission to one or more of the relevant programmes. No separate scholarship application is needed.

#### To be eligible for a scholarship, please note: 

-   You must submit your application for admission no later than March 15 
-   Applicants with the highest score in the online admission test (uniTEST) will be invited to an interview.

-   You must submit your application for admission no later than February 1 - even if you have a Danish residence permit
source.exact_deadline_wording: You must submit your application for admission no later than February 1 - even if you have a Danish residence permit / You must submit your application for admission no later than March 15

Per brief section 6 this is ANNUAL / precision recurring, and the dates were NOT converted into a calendar deadline such as 2027-02-01. Note also that these are admission-application deadlines used for scholarship eligibility, not a separate scholarship deadline: 'No separate scholarship application is needed.'

raw.title: Killam Fellowships Program (Fulbright Canada)
raw.deadline_display: The deadline for the open competition for the 2027-28 Killam Fellowships competition is January 31, 2027.

source.publisher: Fulbright Canada, Foundation for Educational Exchange between Canada and the United States of America
source.as_of: 2027-28 Killam Fellowships competition; page banner reads 'COMPETITION OPEN on AUGUST 15, 2026'
source.raw_extract:
COMPETITION OPEN on AUGUST 15, 2026

The deadline for the open competition for the 2027-28 Killam Fellowships competition is January 31, 2027. If you are a student at one of our partner institutions and you are planning to apply to the direct exchange program, you are encouraged to contact a study abroad advisor at your institution to identify the date on which your institution's internal competition ends. All partner institutions have internal deadlines. Please consult the relevant officials at your home university.
source.exact_deadline_wording: The deadline for the open competition for the 2027-28 Killam Fellowships competition is January 31, 2027.
source.notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE CAVEAT for downstream use: 2027-01-31 is the deadline for the OPEN COMPETITION route only. The Program has two routes and the direct exchange route has no single date - each home institution sets its own internal deadline ('All partner institutions have internal deadlines'). The date was written as EXACT because it is stated explicitly, with a year, on two independent official pages that agree: /americans/application-deadlines and /canadians/application-deadlines, both reading 'January 31, 2027' for the 2027-28 competition, and /americans/how-to-apply ('by January 31st'). No conflict exists between these sources. If the record is meant to represent the whole Program rather than the open competition route, it should be re-scoped to two entries or downgraded to precision 'varies'; the deadline_date above must not be presented as the direct-exchange deadline.

source.exact_deadline_wording: This umbrella record covers all seven MEXT scholarship types (research students, teacher training students, undergraduate students, Japanese studies students, college of technology students, specialized training college students, Young Leaders Program students) under both embassy recommendation and university recommendation. No deadline value of any kind can be established for the programme as a whole.
source.notes: UN-semantics = UNKNOWN is the truthful result here, not a research gap. I fetched the record's official_source_url (https://www.studyinjapan.go.jp, which resolves to the Japanese homepage and carries no scholarship deadline), the catalogue page above, the About Scholarships overview page, and the Flowchart page. None publishes an application date or window. The page explicitly routes timing decisions to embassies, universities and, per the eligibility footnote on the same page, 'Recommendations from official overseas recommending organizations' for YLP. I did not import a date from any single-track guideline PDF in this shard, because per AGENT_BRIEF section 5 a schedule published for a different MEXT track is not evidence for this umbrella record.

The selection process for the PEC-PG program will consist of the following stages:

-   From June 29th to August 13th, Brazilian institutions (HEIs/ICTs) will submit proposals to CNPq.

## When to apply

A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year.

In most cases, you should submit your application between **October** and **January** for courses starting the following academic year.

Each master's website has all the details about the course of study, the list of the participating universities, the entry requirements and all the steps of the application process (with and without scholarship).

Two official Commission sources agree, so this is not CONFLICTING. The window is months only with no day, so MONTH/month is correct and deadline_date is null. raw.deadline_display: To qualify for the Early Bird discount, students must accept their offer of admission and pay the tuition fee, or the first instalment of the tuition fee, by the deadline stated in the admission letter (usually 21 days of the publication of the admission results).

source.publisher: University of Eastern Finland
source.as_of: Page section 'Tuition waivers for 2027 intake', page notes 'Updated on 3 August 2026.'
source.raw_extract:
First academic year (Early Bird discount): To qualify for the Early Bird discount, students must accept their offer of admission and pay the tuition fee, or the first instalment of the tuition fee, by the deadline stated in the admission letter (usually 21 days of the publication of the admission results). If the fee is paid in two equal instalments, the second instalment must be paid by 31 August.

To qualify for the discount, students must accept their offer of admission and pay the tuition fee, or the first instalment of the fee, within 21 days of the publication of the admission results. Detailed payment instructions and the applicable payment deadline will be provided in the admission letter.

Second and subsequent years: The annual tuition fee must be paid by 31 August, either as a single payment or in two equal instalments.
source.exact_deadline_wording: by the deadline stated in the admission letter (usually 21 days of the publication of the admission results)
source.notes: The official page publishes no fixed calendar application deadline for this award. The Early Bird discount is not applied for on a published date: it is triggered by accepting the admission offer and paying within a window that UEF states per admission letter. The only fixed day-month on the page is '31 August', which applies to (a) the second instalment of the first year's tuition fee and (b) the annual tuition fee in second and subsequent years - both are payment obligations, not an application deadline for the award, and neither carries a year, so no date could be written even if it were treated as the deadline. The second/third-year tuition waiver is awarded on academic progress with 'A separate application period is organized after the first year of studies' and no dates published, so no application deadline exists for that part either. Returned as UNKNOWN rather than guessing a date from the Finnish national application cycle, which would be an inference from a different programme. A maintainer who wants to model this record as a recurring 31 August payment obligation can do so from the verbatim quotes above, but that is a modelling choice, not a published application deadline.

source.exact_deadline_wording: ROUND 1 20 April 2026 | ROUND 2 01 June 2026 | ROUND 3 03 August 2026 | ROUND 4 04 September 2026 (January 2027 Intake); ROUND 1 22 October 2026 | ROUND 2 07 December 2026 | ROUND 3 24 February 2027 | ROUND 4 12 April 2027 (August 2027 Intake)
source.notes: This record is a COMPOSITE covering three separate INSEAD programmes (MIM, MBA and MIF), and INSEAD publishes no single deadline for it. I fetched the three official programme scholarship pages directly (insead.edu blocks plain HTTP fetches with 403, so I rendered the live pages in a browser and read the rendered DOM). Findings per programme: (1) MIM - the official MIM scholarships page states only 'To apply for a scholarship, or to be automatically considered for one, you must first start your MIM application.' and ties named scholarships to admission rounds ('Open for all candidates admitted in Rounds 1-3' for Kung Family and Qinqin and Xin Zhang; 'Open for all candidates admitted in Rounds 1-2' for L'Oréal for Youth) with NO calendar date anywhere on the page. (2) MBA - the official MBA scholarships page publishes a Financial Aid Calendar with eight distinct round deadlines across two intakes (January 2027 Intake: 20 April 2026, 01 June 2026, 03 August 2026, 04 September 2026; August 2027 Intake: 22 October 2026, 07 December 2026, 24 February 2027, 12 April 2027). (3) MIF - the official MIF financing page (/master-programmes/master-finance/financing) contains no deadline text at all. Because the record spans three programmes with different (and partly absent) deadlines, per AGENT_BRIEF section 6 this is not a CONFLICTING case - different programmes at the same institution having different deadlines is explicitly not a conflict - and it is not ROLLING either, because no source says 'rolling'. Writing any single one of these eight dates would misrepresent the other seven, so deadline_date stays null and the outcome is a truthful UNKNOWN. Note for the coordinator: four of the eight MBA dates (22 October 2026, 07 December 2026, 24 February 2027, 12 April 2027) are still in the future as of 2026-10-05, so if this record were ever split per programme the MBA August 2027 intake would be genuinely open; I did not select one on the record's behalf. Also note the record's stated official_source_url (the MBA international-funding page) is a lender/scheme directory and contains no deadline at all, so it cannot support any value for this record.

raw.deadline_display: Admitted students can claim the offer by accepting their study place and paying the tuition fee within a deadline specified in their admissions letter. source.publisher: Åbo Akademi University
source.as_of: Page section 'Scholarships for students admitted in 2026 or later'
source.raw_extract:
Scholarships for students admitted in 2026 or later

Åbo Akademi University grants an early commitment offer for students liable to pay tuition fees and who are admitted for studies starting in the autumn of 2026 or later. The early commitment offer is a discount of 4000 €, which means that the remaining tuition fee for the first academic year is 8000 €. Admitted students can claim the offer by accepting their study place and paying the tuition fee within a deadline specified in their admissions letter. Admitted students who do not accept their study place and do not pay the tuition fee within the deadline for the early commitment offer need to pay the full amount of 12000 €.

For the second year, all admitted students are awarded a tuition fee reduction of 4000 €, leaving the remaining annual tuition fee at 8000 €. Applicants do not need to apply separately for this second year scholarship.
source.exact_deadline_wording: within a deadline specified in their admissions letter
source.notes: The official scholarship page publishes NO calendar date for this award. The deadline is explicitly individualised: it is 'a deadline specified in their admissions letter'. I deliberately did NOT write 2027-07-13. I fetched the official application-process page (https://www.abo.fi/en/study/apply/international-master-programmes/application-process/), which does publish a dated 'Admissions timeline 2027' including '13 July 3:00 pm (Helsinki time) Deadline to accept the offered study place' - but that is a generic admissions acceptance deadline, not the scholarship deadline, and the scholarship page itself says the scholarship deadline is the one specified in the admissions letter. Substituting the admissions date for the scholarship deadline is exactly the generic-admissions-deadline substitution the brief bans in section 5, so I rejected it and recorded it here for transparency. The second-year component has no application step at all ('Applicants do not need to apply separately for this second year scholarship'), so it contributes no deadline. I did not classify this ROLLING: although the absence of a public fixed date is functionally close, the source never says 'rolling' or 'no fixed deadline' - it says a real deadline exists and is communicated per admission - so UNKNOWN with precision 'unknown' is the truthful label.

source.notes: This record is a PORTFOLIO record covering a large hub of distinct benefits (ER.GO regional grants, 150-hour collaboration grants, study grants for students experiencing difficulties, international mobility scholarships, fee exemptions, Unibo for Refugees, MUR-CRUI and MAECI scholarships, degree and doctoral awards, and more), each of which is a separate call with its own deadline. Per AGENT_BRIEF section 6, differing deadlines across the different benefits at this one institution are not a conflict, so this is not CONFLICTING. The two quotes above are recorded verbatim so the convention is not lost, but no date is written. A truthful UNKNOWN is the correct result for a portfolio-level record; a per-benefit breakdown would require records that are not in this shard.

source.as_of: live page, retrieved 2026-10-05; no cycle year stated for the scholarship
source.raw_extract: Danish government Scholarships - The University of Copenhagen offers a limited number of tuition waivers and grants through the Danish Government Scholarship programme. ... All non-EU/EEA applicants offered admission will automatically be considered for the scholarship; you do not submit an individual application for the scholarship. | How do we award the scholarship? ... All non-EU/EEA applicants to the University of Copenhagen's MA/MSc degree programmes will automatically be considered for the Danish Government Scholarship, provided they are eligible. Therefore, you do not submit an individual application. | Nominated students receive information directly through the application portal. If you are offered a scholarship, but do not accept it within the specified deadline, the scholarship offer will be revoked, and offered to another applicant. | Faculty of Humanities - All non-EU/EEA students applying for a master's degree programme at the Faculty of Humanities are automatically considered for the Danish Government Scholarships. source.exact_deadline_wording: All non-EU/EEA applicants to the University of Copenhagen’s MA/MSc degree programmes will automatically be considered for the Danish Government Scholarship, provided they are eligible. Therefore, you do not submit an individual application.
source.notes: Fetched the record's official_source_url directly; it is live, and its in-page 'FAQ about Danish Government Scholarships' accordion is included in the quote above. The page publishes NO scholarship application deadline: there is no scholarship application form, so there is no scholarship closing date. The only 'specified deadline' mentioned is an offer-acceptance deadline for nominated students, and the page gives it no date. I deliberately did not use the master's course application deadlines (15 January 23:59 CET for non-EU September intake, etc.) that appear on UCPH's admissions pages: those are the deadline for a different process (the course application) and are inadmissible as this scholarship's deadline. Likewise the Faculty of Theology note about the date for tuition payment 'in the email listing the terms of payment of the tuition fee (sent around mid-May)' is a tuition payment date, not a scholarship application deadline. ROLLING was considered and rejected - the page never says 'rolling' and there is no application window. UNKNOWN is the truthful result; the verbatim 'you do not submit an individual application' wording is preserved in deadline_display so users are not sent looking for a form.

Meeting the deadline

Your admissions application must be submitted by the **funding deadline** specific to your course. The funding deadline is not the same as the application deadline.

The Trust's awarding period runs from the middle of February to the end of July and is an ongoing process throughout that period. source.raw_extract:
Q: What is the overall timeline for requests?

The Residency start date is generally tied to the Fall intake cycle but exceptions may be made mid-year.

-   **November-January** \- Students submit PhD application to partner university and Expression of Interest to Perimeter Institute
-   **February-March** - Universities issue offer letters for September start. Students to upload offer letter(s) to their Expression of Interest application.
-   **April-May** - Perimeter Institute will contact selected students with further details of the Residency program; Students commit to university program and start date
-   **August-September** \- Arrival in Waterloo; beginning of PhD studies

source.notes: Recovered at MONTH precision only, deliberately not dated. Your Expression of Interest must be submitted within one week of submitting your university application (for multiple university applications, use the earliest application date).' So the binding EOI deadline is defined relative to each partner university's own deadline and varies by university; the November-January figure is Perimeter's own cycle overview and is the only Perimeter-published timing.
